items.title: Cerro Verde Copper Coin Honors U.S.-Peru Relations
items.summary: Cerro Verde Copper Coin Honors U.S.-Peru Relations mboyle Sat, 08/08/2026 - 12:10 Post Image August 8, 2026 - A commemorative coin crafted from copper produced at Cerro Verde was unveiled during a recent ceremony at Miami Dade College in Florida, celebrating the bicentennial of diplomatic relations between the United States and Peru. U.S. Ambassador to Peru Bernie Navarro unveiled the copper replica of the official commemorative coin issued by the Central Reserve Bank of Peru. Julia Torreblanca, Senior Vice President of Corporate Affairs-Cerro Verde, was among a group of dignitaries who spoke at the event. Created specifically for the bicentennial celebration, the unique piece was made from 136 pounds of high-purity copper (99.999 percent) produced at Cerro Verde's electrowinning plant in Arequipa. Measuring 35 inches in diameter and almost half an inch thick, the replica of the official coin features two iconic landmarks: Miami, Florida’s Freedom Tower and Peru's Machu Picchu. Peruvian artist Gino Torres transformed the Arequipa copper into a work of historical importance. "Freeport's significant presence in Arequipa reflects a long-term, responsible U.S. investment, thousands of Peruvian jobs and decades of collaboration,” Torreblanca said to those in attendance at the ceremony. “When we were asked to help commemorate 200 years of diplomatic relations between the United States and Peru, we did not hesitate. “This copper comes from Peruvian soil, was produced by proud and responsible miners in Arequipa, shaped by a Peruvian artist and now honors a bond between two nations that continues to grow stronger." Torreblanca also thanked the more than 5,400 Cerro Verde employees and contract workers whose efforts helped make the project possible. She also noted that, in addition to supplying copper and molybdenum, Cerro Verde supports water infrastructure and community development in Arequipa and across Peru.

items.title: Payroll Budgeting in Nigeria: How Businesses Can Plan Salary Costs and Avoid Cash Flow Gaps
items.summary: Finance Payroll Budgeting in Nigeria: How Businesses Can Plan Salary Costs and Avoid Cash Flow Gaps Oluwakemi Adesina August 8, 2026 Payroll budgeting in Nigeria is a step to protecting your cash flow. It is one of your biggest recurring expenses. It stays the same whether sales are up or down, or a client pays late. Skipping payroll planning means salaries are not properly planned for. And when there is growth, like a new hire joining mid-quarter, bonus week, or even remittance season, cash probably runs short. It affects the business operations. The team scrambles to move money rather than run the business. Here is how to build a payroll budget that protects your cash flow. Payroll Processing and Budgeting: The Difference A payroll budget forecasts what you will spend on employee compensation each quarter or year. Payroll processing is paying your team for work already done. It happens at month-end. Payroll budgeting comes first. It asks: What can the business really afford to spend on our workforce over the next year? A business that relies solely on processing experiences headcount growth, statutory updates, and annual bonuses as a series of stressful financial shocks. Conversely, a business that practices proactive workforce budgeting handles these shifts smoothly. The funds are already planned. To make this work, finance and HR teams must break down their organizational silos. HR tracks hiring pipelines, promotions, and exit dates, while finance tracks cash runways and revenue targets. The 6 Layers of a Nigerian Payroll Budget An accurate payroll budget requires looking beyond basic salaries. Most businesses face cash flow gaps because they under-forecast, ignoring hidden variables that increase the total cost of employment. According to international standards, comprehensive salary planning must include all fair compensation parameters, including allowances and statutory protections. To build an airtight forecast, you must implement strict salary cost planning across all six layers of the labor stack: Basic Salaries: This is your baseline. It represents the fixed, non-negotiable monthly cost of your current staff. Contractual Allowances: Under Nigerian labor structures, base pay is often split. You must account for recurring contractual allowances like housing, transport, and utilities specified in employment contracts. Guidelines from the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment outline how these wage components interact with local regulations. Variable Compensations: If your business pays a 13th-month salary, performance bonuses, or sales commissions, these must be forecasted based on performance tiers. Overtime Pay: If you run logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, or retail, overtime matters. Check last year’s data for peak months, such as December. Budget more for overtime in those periods. Statutory Obligations: Compliance costs rise automatically as your team grows. In Nigeria, your budget must factor in pension contributions, the Industrial Training Fund (ITF), and NSITF employee compensation insurance. Skipping these calculations leaves a massive compliance gap in your annual financial layout. Perks and Medical Benefits: Add up the full cost of Group Life Insurance, HMO premiums, staff training, and leave allowances. Step-by-Step Employee Cost Budgeting for Your Business You do not need complex models to build a real forecast. Follow these steps to plan your year: Step 1: Set your baseline. Pull payroll data from the last three months. Add up basic pay, allowances, and statutory costs. This is your current run-rate. Step 2: Layer the Hiring Timeline. Review your company’s growth plans. If HR plans to bring on a new manager in Q3, do not just add their salary to the annual total. Map the full cost stack to start precisely in July. Step 3: Add adjustments. Include promotions, cost-of-living increases, or market corrections. Update your baseline for the exact months these changes start. Step 4: Add Statutory Calculations. Calculate your pension, ITF, and NSITF obligations based on your projected headcount growth, ensuring you use the correct local compliance percentages. Step 5: Add a buffer You cannot predict sudden market changes or emergency hires. Always add a 5%-10% buffer to your monthly allocation to cover unexpected employee expenses. Data security is a key part of administrative safety. When handling financial and personal details during payroll mapping, businesses must ensure security and comply with the Regulations. Why Is Payroll Budgeting Nigeria Critical for Cash Flow? The primary objective of salary budgeting in Nigeria is to protect your liquid cash reserves before payday. A reliable payroll forecasting strategy gives business leaders a clear, three-month runway. When you can see exactly where statutory payments, new hire onboarding, and bonus periods intersect, you gain the foresight to manage cash reserves effectively. You can confidently adjust project timelines, manage vendor payments, or hold back discretionary spending before a crunch happens. Delayed salaries quickly erode employee trust. In the market today, maintaining a reputation for paying on time, every time, is your strongest tool for talent retention. 3 Payroll Budgeting Mistakes Nigerian Businesses Should Avoid The “Set and Forget” Trap A budget is a living document. A plan created in January becomes obsolete by April if your team scales faster than expected or if market realities force salary adjustments. Review the forecast quarterly to keep calculations aligned with reality. 2. Cash Flow Timing Blindspots Your annual calculations might be accurate, but poor timing can still break your business. If annual performance bonuses, insurance renewals, and tax remittances all fall in the same month, you will hit a cash crunch. High payroll expenses in Nigeria must be balanced against real-time cash inflows. 3. Siloed Planning When HR sets hiring targets without cross-checking the finance team’s cash runway, capital strain follows. Finance should never discover a payroll increase on disbursement day. Both teams must collaborate on a unified spreadsheet. Leverage Clean Data for Smarter Budgeting A budget built on guesswork will fail when tested. A budget built on clean historical data; exact overtime trends, clear statutory tracking, and precise headcount costs; is a budget you can confidently defend to partners, board members, or banks. items.title: Employee Retention Strategies in Nigeria: How Businesses Can Reduce Staff Turnover
items.summary: Employee Management Employee Retention Strategies in Nigeria: How Businesses Can Reduce Staff Turnover Oluwakemi Adesina August 8, 2026 Keep your best people next quarter by using the right employee retention strategies for Nigerian businesses. When a trained employee leaves, you lose more than their salary. You lose the training investment, maybe client relationships, and team momentum. When a key employee resigns, the role you spent months filling is vacant again. You restart hiring, onboard a replacement, and hope they stay. Today, skilled staff have more remote and cross-border options than ever. “Hope” does not keep people. Here is what keeps people at Nigerian businesses: why they leave, how pay and payroll drive decisions, and how the right processes put retention in your control. What Is Employee Retention? Employee retention is the ability of your business to keep staff over time. This can be tracked by the basic formula, monitoring some key metrics, and how you organize your data. Retention and engagement are not the same. Engagement is how invested an employee feels in their work. Retention is whether they are still on your payroll in twelve months. An engaged employee can still leave for better pay. A disengaged one may stay because they have no better option. The goal is to keep the right people for the right reasons. Track retention early, as it significantly impacts your overall business operations. If exits cluster in one department or spike at the same tenure, you have a fixable problem in management, pay, or growth. Why Employees Leave Nigerian Companies Most departing employees say they are leaving for new opportunities. Some other reasons are specific and often fixable. Compensation matters, but it is not just about the number. Pay must keep up with the cost of living and market rates. Delayed or inaccurate salaries do more than inconvenience staff. If employees cannot trust their paycheck to arrive on time and in full, they start job hunting. Beyond pay, people leave when they cannot see a future in the role. Talented staff without a path to more responsibility or new skills will look elsewhere. Also, poor management is a factor. Lack of recognition and a disorganized workplace. People quit when managers do not give feedback, take credit for work, or make daily life harder. Employee Retention Strategies Nigeria Businesses Can Use Retention is not one fix. It comes from getting several key things right at once. Pay competitively and pay on time: Benchmark salaries against current market rates, not what you paid three years ago. Guard payment accuracy as closely as you guard the amount. Show employees a clear path forward: Career growth is beyond promotions. It is also a training budget, a defined next role, or a mentor who invests in progress. People stay where they see a future. Make recognition part of daily management: Regular, specific praise and honest feedback drive staff motivation and retention. Offer flexibility where you can: If remote work is not possible, use flexible start times or hybrid schedules. Trusting staff to manage their hours shows respect and respect keeps people. Communicate honestly, especially in tough times: Employees forgive challenges if you tell the truth. They may not forgive silence or surprises. Get onboarding and first-line management right: The first ninety days decide if a new hire sees a future with you. Rushed onboarding and unclear expectations push people out early. Pay, Benefits, and Financial Wellbeing Payroll is more than just admin. It is proof that your business is well run. When salaries are accurate, paid on the same date every month, and backed by a clear pay structure, employees trust you. Payroll errors, even honest ones, destroy that trust fast. Employee retention in Nigeria depends less on the amount and more on whether people can count on getting paid right and on time. Manual payroll leads to mistakes. A missed allowance, wrong deduction, or late payment is noticed instantly because it is your staff’s money. Eazipay removes that risk. We calculate salaries accurately and pay on schedule every time, so your retention efforts are not undone by payroll errors. Beyond salary, Nigerian employees value practical benefits. Health coverage, correct pension contributions, and salary advance options for short-term cash needs show you care about financial wellbeing. How HR Technology Supports Employee Retention Employee retention often fails when it’s not given proper attention. The same HR team spends a lot of time organising data or fixing something. HR technology removes this admin friction, freeing your team to focus on what keeps people: real conversations and real support. Centralized employee records let managers pull up history, leave balance, or compensation details in minutes. Payroll automation removes calculation errors that damage trust. Reliable compliance processes give founders the kind of workforce retention data that flags attrition risk. Nigerian businesses use Eazipay for payroll, employee records, and compliance. HR to focus on what keeps people: real conversations, recognition, and career planning. If you want this for your team, reach out to Eazipay. Frequently Asked Questions What is employee retention? Employee retention is an organization’s ability to keep its employees over a given period, usually measured as a percentage of staff who remain rather than resign. Why is employee retention important? High turnover is expensive and disruptive. It costs time and money to recruit and train replacements, and it disrupts client relationships, team morale, and institutional knowledge that a departing employee takes with them. How can companies reduce employee turnover? Companies reduce employee turnover Nigeria-wide by paying competitively and on time, offering visible career growth, giving regular recognition, allowing reasonable flexibility, communicating honestly, and getting onboarding and first-line management right. Does salary affect employee retention? Yes, though it is rarely just about the amount. Timeliness and accuracy of payment affect trust as much as the figure itself, and a competitive salary that arrives late or wrong still damages retention.
